correctness.rationale: All n>=7 are quantified and branch/measure definitions stated. A positive T1 ladder and explicit positive T4 bridge produce each of n distinct angles; branch inverses give irreducibility. Their nearest unsigned cosine to pi/2 is piecewise sin(abs(t-a/2)), sin(a-t), or sin t according to n mod4. Liouville pushforward has exact density S(t)/2 with finite sine sums, whose Jacobians yield the CDF and first two moments. Numerical checker replay provides 14,036 direct tests plus 44 mass and 88 moment checks, supporting but not replacing the proof. Boundary angles are null; almost-sure infinite trajectory visit assumption is explicit.

Its complete stationary law for every n>=7 yields explicit event probabilities, expected excluded area, a mod-four nonuniformity, and a sharp parity factor-two ratio of essential maximal radii.
